title: Finite rational realization identifies the specified smooth adjunction coefficient comparisons
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$ and a coefficient closure $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ [def-pur-conventions]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be smooth separated of pure relative dimension $d\ge0$, with $X,Y$ separated finite-type $k$-schemes [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. All coefficient fields below are finite subextensions of $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$. Write $\mathcal R_E(W)$ for the raw localization $D^b_c(W,\mathcal O_E)[1/\varpi_E]$ and $C^W_{F/E}$ for its completed-integral scalar transition [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]. Write $\mathcal C_E(W)=\Dctf(W,E)$ for the full bounded constructible finite-Tor subcategory of the ordinary derived category of modules over the pulled-back condensed coefficient sheaf $E_W$ [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. Put $T^W_{F/E}=F_W\otimes^L_{E_W}-$ [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-change].

Use the realization equivalences $R_{E,W}:\mathcal R_E(W)\simeq\mathcal C_E(W)$ with $R_{E,W}K_0=E_W\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_{E,W}}K_0$ and $R_{E,W}(h\otimes e)=e\,h[1/\ell]$, using the integral identification and Hom maps of [sk-lem-integral-models, det-sp-rational-localized-hom]. The integral domain and completed-scalar convention agree with [lem-sf-adic-finite-realization-cocone]. Let
$$\tau^W_{F/E}:R_{F,W}C^W_{F/E}\xrightarrow{\sim}T^W_{F/E}R_{E,W}$$
be the comparison defined by the inverse of the quotient-tower augmentation $\chi$ of [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison] followed by balanced tensor multiplication, as in that cocone.

Let $P_E,J_E$ be raw compact supports and raw $Lf^*(-)(d)[2d]$, with the detailed Tate twists [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support, def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. Let $P^c_E=Rf_{!,E}$ be the actual ordinary condensed compactification composite $R\bar f_*j_!$ and $J^c_E=Lf_E^*(-)\otimes^L E_X(d)[2d]$, with the condensed Tate line of [sk-def-sp-tate-twist]. There are canonical natural isomorphisms
$$u_{E,M}:R_{E,Y}P_EM\xrightarrow{\sim}P^c_ER_{E,X}M,\qquad v_{E,K}:R_{E,X}J_EK\xrightarrow{\sim}J^c_ER_{E,Y}K.$$
Here $u$ uses the compact-support localization comparison of [det-sp-rational-localized-hom], with the completed-tower compact-support identification of [lem-pur-compact-support-condensed-realization]. The map $v$ uses the pullback localization comparison and the identification of the detailed integral Tate line with the condensed line: on a cover with compatible Kummer generators $\zeta_n$ it sends the integral generator to the identical sequence $\zeta_n$, then localizes and tensors $d$ times. Thus it is an identification of these specified twists, including their finite scalar transitions, and commutes with pullback composition, tensor associators and shifts.

Let $b^r:C^Y_{F/E}P_E\simeq P_FC^X_{F/E}$ and $a^r:C^X_{F/E}J_E\simeq J_FC^Y_{F/E}$ be precisely the raw comparisons of [sk-lem-sp-field-extension]. Let $b^c:T^Y_{F/E}P^c_E\simeq P^c_FT^X_{F/E}$ be the ambient compact-support scalar comparison of [det-prop-scalar-six-compact-support], and let $a^c:T^X_{F/E}J^c_E\simeq J^c_FT^Y_{F/E}$ be the pullback, balanced tensor and same-root twist comparison [det-prop-scalar-six-pullback, sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients]. Composition is right to left. These actual maps satisfy
$$b^c_{R_{E,X}M}\,T^Y_{F/E}(u_{E,M})\,\tau^Y_{F/E,P_EM}=P^c_F(\tau^X_{F/E,M})\,u_{F,C^X_{F/E}M}\,R_{F,Y}(b^r_M),$$
$$a^c_{R_{E,Y}K}\,T^X_{F/E}(v_{E,K})\,\tau^X_{F/E,J_EK}=J^c_F(\tau^Y_{F/E,K})\,v_{F,C^Y_{F/E}K}\,R_{F,X}(a^r_K).$$

Let $\alpha^r_E:P_E\dashv J_E$ be the raw adjunction obtained by tensoring the integral tower Hom bijection of [det-sp-integral-adjunction-bijection] with $E$, with unit $\eta^r_E$ and counit $t^r_E$. Let $\alpha^c_E$ be the condensed Hom bijection obtained from that same integral bijection by the two localized-Hom maps of [det-sp-rational-localized-hom] and the displayed endpoints, with unit $\eta^c_E$ and counit $t^c_E$. For every raw arrow $h:P_EM\to K$ one has the equality of specified bijections
$$\alpha^c_E\bigl(R_{E,Y}(h)\,u_{E,M}^{-1}\bigr)=v_{E,K}\,R_{E,X}\bigl(\alpha^r_E(h)\bigr).$$
In particular
$$t^c_{E,R_{E,Y}K}\,P^c_E(v_{E,K})\,u_{E,J_EK}=R_{E,Y}(t^r_{E,K}),$$
$$\eta^c_{E,R_{E,X}M}=J^c_E(u_{E,M})\,v_{E,P_EM}\,R_{E,X}(\eta^r_{E,M}).$$
Consequently the raw Hom, unit and counit compatibility of [sk-lem-sp-field-extension] becomes compatibility for these very condensed $a^c,b^c$, rather than for arbitrarily chosen endpoint isomorphisms.

Finally, for $E\subset F\subset L$, let $\sigma^r:C_{L/F}C_{F/E}\simeq C_{L/E}$ and $\sigma^c:T_{L/F}T_{F/E}\simeq T_{L/E}$ be the specified scalar associators. On either scheme the realization comparisons satisfy
$$\tau_{L/E}\,R_L(\sigma^r)=\sigma^c_{R_E}\,T_{L/F}(\tau_{F/E})\,\tau_{L/F,C_{F/E}}.$$
Under this equation the raw cocycles for $a^r,b^r$ identify with the condensed cocycles for $a^c,b^c$; identity extensions identify with the coefficient unitors. All assertions concern finite coefficient fields only; they assume the raw integral-localized adjunction and its raw compatibility, and impose no additional condensed compatibility hypothesis.

Agent-formulated interface obligation: identify those particular raw comparisons with ordinary condensed scalar/pullback-twist comparisons. Current sk-thm-purity-transport proof Steps 2 and 4; inherited main-20261015 Step 3: transitive in coefficient extensions.

proof.text: Use [lem-sf-adic-finite-realization-cocone] to identify the completed integral domains, their actual morphisms and reductions, and their raw localizations. Its realization and the Hom formula of [det-sp-rational-localized-hom] give exactly the stated $R_{E,W}$: on a rational arrow $h\otimes e$ it is $e\,h[1/\ell]$. Its scalar isomorphism $j$ is the stated $\tau$, since both use the inverse of the same quotient augmentation $\chi$ followed by multiplication. Here [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison] supplies an isomorphism on complete inputs, including ramified extensions; no quotient coefficient map is presumed flat. These are identifications of functors and maps, not replacements of the raw category by a condensed definition. Since $\Dctf(W,\mathcal O_E)=\Dbc(W,\mathcal O_E)$ [sk-lem-integral-models] and derived scalar extension preserves Tor-amplitude intervals, every $R_{E,W}K_0$ has finite Tor amplitude over $E_W$; hence the essential image is the full subcategory $\mathcal C_E(W)$ of the statement.

source.place: Finite-free coefficient extension on reduction towers, then inversion of ell; expanded agent argument for the specified condensed endpoints and their scalar normalization.

proof.text: Identify the two integral Tate lines before localizing. By [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free], the detailed line is $Z_W\otimes_{\widehat{\mathbf Z}_{\ell,W}}\mathcal O_{E,W}$, where $Z_W=\lim_r\mu_{\ell^r,W}$. In [sk-def-sp-tate-twist] the condensed integral line has coordinates $\mu_{\ell^n,W}\otimes(\mathcal O_E/\ell^n)_W$. Map the detailed line to this limit by its quotient maps. On a compatible-root cover both sides are the completed coefficient sheaf and this map is $a\mapsto(\zeta_n\otimes\bar a)_n$, hence is invertible. This is a map of sheaves defined globally by the projections; local checking here concerns sheaf maps, not equality of arbitrary derived maps. The cofinal identification $\ell^n\mathcal O_E=\varpi_E^{en}\mathcal O_E$ retains all projections. Under a change $\zeta_n\mapsto\zeta_n^{c_n}$ both trivializations change by the same compatible unit, so the map is independent of the roots. The finite-extension maps agree by [lem-weil-integral-twist-base-change] and the coordinate formulas in the condensed definition. Tensor this sheaf isomorphism $d$ times and invert $\ell$ to obtain exactly the specified $E_W(d)$ identification; for $d=0$ it is the coefficient identity.

source.place: Finite-free coefficient extension on reduction towers, then inversion of ell; expanded agent argument for the specified condensed endpoints and their scalar normalization.

proof.text: For $M$ represented by $M_0$, define $u$ as the compact-support localization comparison of [det-sp-rational-localized-hom], with the integral compact-support identification of [lem-pur-compact-support-condensed-realization]. Inside $u$, $P_EM_0\cong R\bar f_*j_!M_0$ is the canonical isomorphism of [det-sp-integral-direct-image-tower](2), the one used for the compact-support endpoint of [lem-pur-rationalized-smooth-adjunction-diagrams] in Step 6. The realization theorem's $\alpha$ evaluates to the maps induced by the same total-limit projections ($\ell^n$ and $\varpi_E^n$ towers being cofinal), so the two integral identifications give the same map of reduction towers and coincide, reduction being an equivalence on $\Dbc(-,\mathcal O_E)$ [det-sp-normalized-equivalence]. Thus $u$ is both $a_{f,E}$ and the Step 6 endpoint. The realization theorem identifies the actual strict-tower compact supports, their finite scalar comparisons, and the condensed projection comparison, retaining coefficient composition coherences. The raw $b^r$ is the localization of that tower comparison by [det-sp-field-extension-towers]. Its completed normalization is explicitly $P_F(\chi_X)b^t\chi_Y^{-1}$ in [lem-pur-integral-coefficient-model-comparison]. Substituting $\tau=\mathrm{mult}\circ R_F(\chi^{-1})$ cancels these two completion factors. The remaining square is precisely the scalar/projection square of the compact-support realization theorem. Its condensed comparison is the proper direct-image comparison followed by the open tensor comparison, the composite specifying $b^c$ in [det-prop-scalar-six-compact-support]. Thus it gives the first displayed equation with $b^c,T(u),\tau$ on the left and $P_F^c(\tau),u_F,R_F(b^r)$ on the right, with exactly their stated endpoints. Naturality extends from integral arrows to $h\otimes e$ since all maps are linear and both routes multiply by the same image of $e$.

proof.text: The pullback localization comparison of [det-sp-rational-localized-hom], followed by the Tate identification of Step 2, defines $v$. Tensoring with the integral Tate line can be computed without completion: [lem-pur-integral-line-reduction-restriction] identifies its ordinary and completed tensors on complete objects. For the pullback portion of the finite scalar square, use [lem-pur-framework-pbc-pullback-scalar-bridge](2),(4): conjugating the actual strict-tower pullback comparison by $\chi^{-1}$ gives ordinary tensor/pullback reassociation followed by the completion comparison, and the same equation holds after raw localization. In the ordinary condensed categories this reassociation is the specified inverse-image/scalar comparison: [lem-sfb-internal-scalar-pullback-normalization] identifies its internal and section-module maps on K-flat representatives, and [det-prop-scalar-six-pullback](1),(3) supplies its composition coherence. After the localization comparison all scalar-association factors multiply in the order $b\otimes(a\otimes x)\mapsto ba\otimes x$. Thus this square uses the stated $\tau$ and the actual condensed pullback comparison, with no independently chosen natural automorphism inserted.

source.place: Finite-free coefficient extension on reduction towers, then inversion of ell; expanded agent argument for the specified condensed endpoints and their scalar normalization.

proof.text: Insert the Tate line into the pullback square of Step 4. The raw twist comparison is the localization of [lem-weil-integral-twist-derived-scalar]; on flat representatives it sends $(x\otimes l)\otimes b$ to $(x\otimes b)\otimes(l\otimes1)$, conjugated by the specified $\chi$. By Step 2 the image of $l$ is the same-root condensed line element. The ordinary derived line comparison of [lem-pur-ordinary-line-derived-scalar-comparison] has exactly this formula and retains arbitrary derived morphisms and coefficient associators. Hence the twist squares commute before deriving, and the normalized derived comparison in that theorem gives the required equality after deriving. The raw comparison in [det-sp-field-extension-towers](3) is this pullback/twist comparison. The line pullbacks are those of [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients]. The derived monoidal composition comparisons [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons] and the shift constraints [lem-pur-derived-tensor-additive-constraints] retain tensor associators, pullback composition and shifts; the line has degree zero, and $2d$ is even. Composing these squares gives exactly the second displayed equation, namely $a^cT(v)\tau=J_F^c(\tau)v_FR_F(a^r)$. This also proves all the asserted naturality and structural compatibilities of $v$.

proof.text: Write $\Phi_E$ for the integral smooth Hom bijection obtained from [det-sp-integral-adjunction-bijection] using its purity isomorphism. By [lem-pur-rationalized-smooth-adjunction-diagrams], $\Phi_E$ and its inverse are $\mathcal O_E$-linear, the raw bijection is $\Phi_E\otimes E$, and the specified localized-Hom construction is $\rho_X(\Phi_E\otimes1)\rho_Y^{-1}$. The endpoint maps in that assertion are the compact-support and pullback localization maps and tensor reassociation of the integral Tate line. Steps 2--5 identify these with exactly $u,v$, including the same-root line rather than an arbitrary isomorphism. For $h=\sum_i h_i\otimes e_i$, both the raw construction and the condensed one therefore give $\sum_i e_i\Phi_E(h_i)[1/\ell]$ under these endpoints. Thus $\alpha_E^c(R_E(h)u_M^{-1})=v_KR_E(\alpha_E^r(h))$. The Hom isomorphisms of [det-sp-rational-localized-hom] make this independent of the chosen tensor expression, and naturality makes it independent of presentations of condensed objects by lattices.

proof.text: For the unit set $K=P_EM$ and $h=1_{P_EM}$ in Step 6. It gives $\alpha_E^c(u_M^{-1})=v_{P_EM}R_E(\eta_M^r)$. Naturality of the Hom bijection in its target gives $\alpha_E^c(1_{P_E^cR_EM})=J_E^c(u_M)\alpha_E^c(u_M^{-1})$, proving the unit formula. For the counit set $M=J_EK$ and $h=t_K^r$. Since $\alpha_E^r(t_K^r)=1_{J_EK}$, Step 6 says $\alpha_E^c(R_E(t_K^r)u_{J_EK}^{-1})=v_K$. The inverse Hom bijection sends $v_K$ to $t^c_{R_EK}P_E^c(v_K)$. Multiply the resulting equality on the right by $u_{J_EK}$ to obtain the stated counit formula. These are direct applications of the definitions of the unit and counit; all arrows have the stated domains.

proof.text: Apply the raw unit/counit compatibility of [sk-lem-sp-field-extension]. Replace $R(P_E-)$ and $R(J_E-)$ by their endpoints using $u,v$, and replace raw scalar passages using $\tau$. Step 3 replaces the resulting compact-support comparison by $b^c$, and Step 5 replaces the twisted-pullback comparison by $a^c$. In each identity the adjacent $u^{-1}u$, $v^{-1}v$ and $\tau^{-1}\tau$ cancel by naturality, while Step 7 identifies the unit and counit themselves. Hence these very $a^c,b^c$ preserve the condensed unit and counit. Hom compatibility follows as well by writing an adjunct as $J(h)\eta$ (or an inverse adjunct as $tP(-)$) and using that naturality. This step transfers already proved equations; it assumes no condensed compatibility.

proof.text: Finally [lem-sf-adic-finite-realization-cocone] states the successive-extension equation for its actual $j=\tau$, with the balanced multiplication $g\otimes(f\otimes(e\otimes x))\mapsto gfe\otimes x$. In the present notation this is exactly $\tau_{L/E}R_L(\sigma^r)=\sigma^c_{R_E}T_{L/F}(\tau_{F/E})\tau_{L/F,C_{F/E}}$. Conjugate the two raw cocycle identities of [sk-lem-sp-field-extension] by $u,v$. Use the two equations proved in Steps 3 and 5 and this equation for $\tau$; successive inverse/comparison pairs cancel, leaving respectively the condensed $b^c$ and $a^c$ cocycles. The identity case of the cocone is multiplication by $1$, so the same cancellation gives the coefficient unitors. Every coefficient appearing in these calculations is a finite extension. No passage to algebraically closed coefficients or additional adjunction is used.
